newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF confirms interest in GAN insurance.
newsitem.headline: AGF confirms interest in GAN insurance.

text.p: French insurer AGF said on Wednesday it was keen to buy state-controlled GAN's core insurance operations to increase its market clout following the mega-merger of two rival insurers, Axa and UAP.
"AGF is definitely interested in buying GAN's insurance operations," said a spokesman for AGF, ending months of speculation about the intentions of France's No. 2 insurer.
Axa's takeover last year of UAP, creating the largest insurer on the domestic scene and the second biggest worldwide, has put strong pressure on AGF to boost its position.

An official record of testimony by AGF chairman Antoine Jeancourt-Galignani to a Senate hearing said he made a strong pitch for Assurances Generales de France (AGF) to take over GAN. Without GAN, "he would not give much for AGF's independence within two or three years," the account said.
AGF, privatised last year, said it would not be interested in GAN's beleaguered UIC property lending arm or its CIC regional banking network, which the centre-right government will sell separately.
The government will pump 20 billion francs ($3.4 billion) into GAN, forced to take repeated provisions to cover huge property losses, mainly at UIC, to ready it for sale this year.
GAN, hit by France's long-running property slump and an ill-fated pricing strategy, reported a 5.7 billion franc loss for 1996, up from 1.79 billion in 1995.
AGF's 1996 profits rose 42 percent to 1.54 billion francs.

Jeancourt-Galignani said earlier this year that GAN's "management had made a very complete inventory of the losses and problems of GAN" and that GAN could look forward to a future as a "normal player" in the insurance sector.

Moves to privatise GAN have been put on hold by the two-round French parliamentary election to be held May 25 and June 1 but a source said there was a lot of behind-the-scenes activity involving the Treasury, AGF and GAN.
The centre-right has pledged to continue its privatisation programme if it is re-elected.
The opposition Socialists, which polls indicate are closing the gap on the conservatives, have vowed to keep all public service companies under government control.

But they have said they will take a "pragmatic" approach to state-controlled companies which operate "in the competitive sector which do not have a public service role and where state participation is no longer necessary."

AGF believes the amount of public money being poured into GAN means it would be more "politically correct" to sell it to a French company rather than a foreign insurer, said the source, who is close to the two companies.
German insurer Allianz has been mentioned as a possible candidate to buy GAN to extend its French presence.

AGF also believes the fact it was privatised last year would make its corporate culture much closer to that of GAN than to bank Worms' insurance unit Athena, which has also been mentioned as a possible AGF bid target, the Senate account said.

Referring to speculation AGF itself could be a bid target, Jeancourt-Galignani said any offer would be "necessarily hostile which is quite unusual and pretty difficult to pull off in the insurance sector," the Senate record said.
The possiblity AGF will take over GAN has caused some disquiet among analysts as AGF has not had the same experience in takeovers as Axa which has grown through acquisitions.
GAN shares finished down 0.29 percent at 136.20 francs after being up more nearly four percent earlier in the day. AGF was off 0.89 percent at 190.60 francs.
